::::{#thm-penalized-least-squares}
#### Penalized least squares has a closed-form solution

Let $\mat{B}$ be an $n \times q$ basis matrix (built as in @def-basis-expansion),
$\vy$ an $n \times 1$ outcome vector,
$\mat{P}$ a symmetric, positive semidefinite $q \times q$ penalty matrix,
and $\l \ge 0$,
and suppose that $\tp{\mat{B}}\mat{B} + \l \mat{P}$ is invertible.
Then the unique minimizer of the penalized residual sum of squares

$$
\text{PRSS}_\l(\vb)
\eqdef \tp{(\vy - \mat{B}\vb)} (\vy - \mat{B}\vb) + \l \tp{\vb} \mat{P} \vb
$$

is

$$
\ub{\evb_\l}_{q \times 1}
= \ub{\paren{\tp{\mat{B}}\mat{B} + \l \mat{P}}^{-1}}_{q \times q}
\ub{\tp{\mat{B}}}_{q \times n} \ub{\vy}_{n \times 1},
$$

and the fitted values are $\est{\vy} = \mat{S}_\l \vy$, with smoother matrix

$$
\ub{\mat{S}_\l}_{n \times n}
\eqdef \ub{\mat{B}}_{n \times q}
\ub{\paren{\tp{\mat{B}}\mat{B} + \l \mat{P}}^{-1}}_{q \times q}
\ub{\tp{\mat{B}}}_{q \times n}
$$

[@wood2017generalized, §4.2; @hastie2009esl2e, §5.4].
::::
